cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 takes up T3's reservoir: useless without the flow.
cells.limitation: T2, T5, T8 ignore the physics turns; alternating monologues across the three minds.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T4 adds the stock versus flow distinction to T3's reservoir.
cells.limitation: No later turn uses T4's distinction; T6 and T9 restate T3.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T7 mentions surface winds as an input.
cells.limitation: Prevailing westerlies, west versus east coast, Labrador Current never raised anywhere.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T8 links T7's feedback loops to land use.
cells.limitation: T8 I agree is unearned; no view reshapes another through T9.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D separates the reservoir from dynamic oceanic flow.
cells.limitation: Ending gives no clearer account of the Europe versus Canada gap; T9 repeats T3.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 grants T3's reservoir point with True before qualifying.
cells.limitation: Strongest physical explanation never stated; T6 ignores T5 entirely.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 objects a reservoir is useless without the flow.
cells.limitation: T5 and T9 assert rather than test assumptions; T6 never answers T4.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T9 on water's thermal capacity stabilising coastal climate is accurate.
cells.limitation: T5, T8 present human land use as a cause; Diamond attribution suspected.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T7 frames salinity and wind change conditionally.
cells.limitation: T5 asserts Europe developed differently because of climate as settled fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T8 concedes T7's point about differing feedback loops.
cells.limitation: T9 dismisses T8 without answering it; no claim revised in nine turns.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A notes doubt whether ocean currents are the sole cause.
cells.limitation: Sections A and E recast a physics question as physical versus historical preference.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 addresses the Gulf Stream assumption behind the question.
cells.limitation: Winter and similar latitudes never shape any argument; no places named.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E points to AMOC for the physical side.
cells.limitation: Section E substitutes if you prioritize for the user's goal of an explanation.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T6 names latitude, elevation and proximity to sea.
cells.limitation: Section A invents a human adaptation tension absent from the question.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches, but only on the user's preference.
cells.limitation: Which European places or which Canadian coast is never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section A guesses the user doubts the ocean-current explanation.
cells.limitation: One motive asserted in Section A; no alternatives, no question to the user.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T1 surfaces the Gulf Stream as sole cause assumption.
cells.limitation: No turn tests how much the Gulf Stream contributes; T9 restates T3.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section E contrasts physical and historical framings.
cells.limitation: Nothing shows why either framing matters to the user's understanding.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T1 names the habit of isolating the Gulf Stream.
cells.limitation: Popular textbook framing raised in T1 is never examined afterwards.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E offers two lines of further reading.
cells.limitation: No distinction the user could test; Section E reduces it to preference.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section D names reservoir and dynamic oceanic flow explanations.
cells.limitation: Atmospheric heat transport by westerlies never defined as a competing explanation.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T4 notes the reservoir explanation lacks a flow mechanism.
cells.limitation: No explanation's evidential cost stated in any turn or section.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: None; Section E ends on what the user prioritizes.
cells.limitation: No observable fact, e.g. west versus east coasts, separates explanations.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section D notes the human role remains disputed.
cells.limitation: Main unknown, ocean versus atmosphere share, never separated from minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Section E suggests researching the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation.
cells.limitation: Section E's historical climate adaptation studies do not bear on the question.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T6 plain list: latitude, elevation, proximity to the sea.
cells.limitation: T1, T7 feedback loops and equilibrium point left abstract and unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 a reservoir clearly points to T3.
cells.limitation: T8 I agree could refer to T7 or T6; claims rarely cite turns.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine short turns, quick to read.
cells.limitation: T6 is 24 words, under the 25-word floor per runner check.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Classical Observer stays on physical law in T3, T6, T9.
cells.limitation: No explicit change of position; one formal register across all minds.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns are brief with no long recaps.
cells.limitation: T6 and T9 restate T3; Section E repeats Section D's split.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T1 challenges the single-cause Gulf Stream story.
cells.limitation: Physics versus history tension in T2, T5 is invented, not from the issue.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T1 opens by denying the Gulf Stream is the sole cause.
cells.limitation: No reversal anywhere; T8 agreement names no cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T3 great regulator, reservoir of heat has period flavour.
cells.limitation: Systems Analyst and Historical Contextualist speak in flat, interchangeable register.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T4 a reservoir is useless without the flow.
cells.limitation: No vivid example such as two named coastal cities anywhere.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T4's challenge briefly raises the pace.
cells.limitation: Even tone throughout; T9 ends where T3 began.

strengths: T4 gives the one real development: a reservoir of heat matters only with flow.
T1 opens by questioning the popular Gulf Stream as sole cause story.
T6 and T9 name proximity to sea and water's thermal capacity, accurate partial causes.
weaknesses: Section E recasts an explanation question as a preference between physical and historical framings.
No mind raises prevailing westerlies, west versus east coast, or the Labrador Current.
Historical Contextualist in T2, T5, T8 shifts to human development, irrelevant to the winter gap.

symptoms.observed: Section E ends on user preference; no observable fact separates the explanations.
symptoms.evidence: If you prioritize the physical mechanism, the answer lies in

symptoms.observed: Wind direction and coast position never raised; debate stays on oceans versus humans.
symptoms.evidence: the salinity or the surface winds

symptoms.observed: Human land use and development presented as shaping the climate gap without support.
symptoms.evidence: influencing local microclimates through agriculture and urbanization

symptoms.observed: Classical Observer restates the land and water point three times without development.
Physics question turned into a physical versus historical framing contest.
symptoms.evidence: shaped how we perceive their climates

findings.description: Human adaptation and land use offered as a contested co-cause of the Europe versus Canada winter gap with no support.
Explanation omits prevailing westerly winds carrying maritime air to Europe and continental air to eastern Canada, a central cause.
Guns, Germs, and Steel does not appear to address Europe versus Canada winter climate or perception of it.
Unquoted Guyot paraphrases may not match The Earth and Man text.
T6 has 24 words, under the 25-word range, per deterministic check.

rubric_fit_notes: Misfit_slot applies to Section E, which has no turn number. The westerlies omission is judged from domain knowledge, so it is reported as suspected. Criterion 4 cells fit an explanation question loosely; rated on assumptions about the topic.
raw.question_type_note: Read as exploratory: C5 scored on separating competing explanations, and Section E's preference framing cost C3.1 and C5.3.
